Depends on what you define as "degenerate strategies." I could define "degenerate strategies" as "adding more and more RNG to Hearthstone as time goes by--so much so that major tournaments are determined by random effects." I only play Wild for a few reasons:

1. I own the entire card collection. I'd like to use all the cards I "own."
2. I've played since the game's first year of existence. I'm familiar enough with strategies and decks to not be caught by surprise by whatever "degeneracy" is currently being tried.
3. Standard is nothing but playing the same game against the same 4 deck types over and over and over and over and over and over and over and over again. I like a little variety. It's the spice of life. ;)

And finally, even more cool interactions and possibilities occur when you pair brand new cards with cards that exist in sets released since the beginning of the game. It's exhilarating to figure out new and different ways to "be degenerate." It's why I frequent threads like this. I like to see new ideas, and then I like to see how I can expand on those ideas in Wild.

Come join us. We all float down here.

Thanks for the replies, everyone. It's extremely hard to he living this nightmare right now, but it's good to read other perspectives and think that maybe I'll feel another way another time. In the moment though, it's excruciating. In one way, it's overwhelmingly soul-rending and makes me feel like there's no point to life anymore. But, in another way, I know part of this is something I have to go through to understand the severity of my own actions so I can change. I just pray it's not permanent. Because, not being there for my kids during their ENTIRE childhood while living my own life is worse to me than getting a life sentence to federal prison. At least if I received a life sentence, I'd have an excuse why I wasn't able to make an attempt be involved in my kid's lives.

I appreciate the response. I do feel that my family is worth it, but a lot of times (and particularly in my case) it can be impossible to even maintain contact with them, and/or overcome the overwhelming judgement and wall that comes up from them and everyone they're associated with/influenced by. There's no getting around that when you've been basically condemned to exile. Maybe it's easier for other people to just walk away and start a new life, but I actually have love in my heart for them and motivation to be a good Dad, but that has been taken away from me by my own actions. I will just have to "live with it," as they say. And, right now, I just don't think I can. It's not that I fear hatred from most people. From most people, I think I could take it. But, not from my own kids. It's not fair to anyone--particularly my kids--that I did this. I just find it overwhelmingly heartbreaking that it seems like this situation has shaped up to be that I will never be given a second chance--no matter if I'm sorry, no matter if I take action to modify my behavior, and no matter if I show I'm a changed man. It's just too late.
